title: The vacuum--fourth-chaos Ritz vector has an order-sigma_N higher-chaos residual and is not a ground-state quasimode

nonquasimode_boundary.ritz_vector: Let u_N=alpha_N 1+beta_N X_N be K1484's normalized lower Ritz vector, with alpha_N->1/sqrt(2), beta_N->-1/sqrt(2)
nonquasimode_boundary.higher_chaos_test: For K_N^proj=H0+g sigma_N X_N, test the residual against K1488's unit vector Y_N orthogonal to 1 and X_N
nonquasimode_boundary.interaction_residual: <Y_N,g sigma_N X_N u_N>=g sigma_N beta_N tau_N with tau_N>=1
nonquasimode_boundary.free_residual: X_N has chaos degree four and Y_N degree at most eight, so Cauchy--Schwarz and H0<=d omega_max on degree d give |<Y_N,H0 X_N>|=O(omega_max(N))=O(N)
nonquasimode_boundary.residual_lower_bound: Because sigma_N=Theta(N^(5/2)), ||(K_N^proj-lambda_N^-)u_N||>=g sigma_N/3 for all sufficiently large N
nonquasimode_boundary.consequence: The two-dimensional lower Ritz vector is not a quasimode at any error o(sigma_N), and its coefficient -1 cannot be promoted to the leading full ground-energy correction
nonquasimode_boundary.ceiling: The residual proves instability of the two-dimensional truncation, not a matching many-chaos lower bound, exact ground-energy scale or absence of a localized true ground state
